- If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid bearish overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the 10–15 day horizon; apply a +1.5–2.5% bias to 10–15 day forecasts.  
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, model often fails to capture momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for 7–10 day horizon.  
- Model shows strong lag in reacting to sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive after 3 days, adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead to reflect the shift.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate the final 5–7 days; apply a +1–2% correction to the last 5–7 days of the forecast.
